sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: when to brake and when not to, anti-lock versus ordinary brakes, rear-end versus head-on crashes, fire suppression, skid steering and animals
Look-alike emergency responses from the vehicle emergency and crash-avoidance pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec21-R01 | anchor: A01
During a blowout you do not brake until the car is almost stopped, and only then do you signal, pull off and apply the brakes. [A01]
Why it matters: group blowouts; difficulty two; confusable sec21-F06 versus sec21-F07.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-R02 | anchor: A01
A vehicle fire calls for an ABC dry chemical extinguisher, or a heavy blanket, coat or sand, but never water on burning gasoline. [A01]
Why it matters: group fires; difficulty two; confusable sec21-F10 versus sec21-F11 versus sec21-F12.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-R03 | anchor: A01
With an overheated engine you raise the hood but keep the radiator cap on, and you add water only once the engine has cooled. [A01]
Why it matters: group overheating; difficulty two; confusable sec21-F16 versus sec21-F17.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec21-R04 | anchor: A02
Anti-lock brakes should not be pumped, while failed ordinary brakes should be pumped rapidly to build pressure. [A02]
Why it matters: group brake failure; difficulty three; confusable sec21-F23 versus sec21-F24.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-R05 | anchor: A02
Before a rear-end hit you release the brake an instant before impact, while before a head-on crash you slow down and head for the shoulder. [A02]
Why it matters: group crash avoidance; difficulty three; confusable sec21-F28 versus sec21-F30.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-R06 | anchor: A02
When the engine dies in a turn, the steering response is to grip with both hands and finish the turn, while the braking response is to press extra hard if the car has power brakes. [A02]
Why it matters: group power steering; difficulty two; prereq sec21-F18.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-R07 | anchor: A02
When the parking brake is used for a brake failure, you hold the release so you can let off if the rear wheels lock. [A02]
Why it matters: group brake failure; difficulty three; prereq sec21-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec21-R08 | anchor: A03
In a skid you steer toward where you want to go, which is the direction of the skid, and then steer back as the car straightens. [A03]
Why it matters: group skids; difficulty three; confusable sec21-F37 versus sec21-F38.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-R09 | anchor: A03
When two hazards cannot be separated, the extra room goes to the most likely danger, such as a child on a bike rather than oncoming cars. [A03]
Why it matters: group compromise; difficulty two; prereq sec21-F34.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-R10 | anchor: A03
An animal already on the road calls for slowing and steering around it without losing control, while an animal beside the road calls for not honking. [A03]
Why it matters: group animals; difficulty two; confusable sec21-F43 versus sec21-F44.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec21-R11 | anchor: A03
Swerving hard to miss road debris is a common cause of run-off-road crashes, and sometimes driving over the debris is the less severe choice. [A03]
Why it matters: group debris; difficulty two; prereq sec21-F40.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]
